subject: Pricing escalation: OptimaHealth Dedicated pool — counterproposal request
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25 09:12 PDT
Subject: OptimaHealth dedicated ask — pricing ask for exec exception

Marissa,

Quick summary from last call with OptimaHealth (Susan + procurement): they want a 12-month reserved commit for a 4xA100-equivalent GPU pool (steady throughput for inference pipelines) with an option to scale up for batch training bursts. Their procurement ask: 35% off list and two months of free burst credits to cover expected onboarding traffic. They cited a competitive offer from LargeCloud that includes a 30% off baseline and a technical SLA for throughput at scale.

Attached is the initial estimate (Optima_Initial_Estimate_20270425.pdf). They are strategic in healthcare analytics (HIPAA-adjacent) and could be a strong reference for private deployments.

Can we get a pricing exception path here? If we can't do 35%, what's the maximum concession we can push that won't set a broad precedent? Also flagging that they asked for a throughput SLO (tokens/day) tied to credits.

—Aditya
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25 11:05 PDT
Subject: RE: OptimaHealth dedicated ask — pricing ask for exec exception

Vivek / Tessa —

I pulled together negotiation background and a proposed counteroffer: 25% off list pricing for the 12-month reserved commit, plus one month of free burst credits (150k token equivalent) up front to smooth onboarding. We would include a throughput SLO of 10M tokens/day with a rollback policy (if SLO missed more than 2 times in a quarter they can apply credits).

Why this structure: 25% keeps us within our mid-tier concession band, preserves margin vs a straight 35% discount, and gives a tangible operational remedy (credits) rather than a permanent price concession. It also buys time to operationalize their private VPC onboarding and validate performance.

Attached is a draft offer for your review (Optima_Dedicated_Offer_20270425.pdf). If you're comfortable with the structure, I'd like to present this to Optima by EOD.

Marissa
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25 15:30 PDT
Subject: RE: OptimaHealth dedicated ask — pricing ask for exec exception

Marissa / Aditya —

Approve in principle. I will ok a 25% discount + one month free burst credits, conditional on the following:
- Finance signs off on ARR impact vs CAC assumptions (I need a 12-month cashflow table).
- Legal signs the SLO language with credit-trigger mechanics and an explicit limit on escalation applicability.

Please route the revised rate card and the CLM/DocuSign link to me once Finance/Legal stamp it. I am putting an exec sign-off token on this: EX-2027-344.

One ask: make the burst credit non-transferable and visible on the first invoice so procurement can reconcile.

Vivek
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Lee <susan.lee@optimahealth.com>, procurement@optimahealth.com
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-26 08:50 PDT
Subject: OptimaHealth counteroffer: Dedicated reserved pool — Redwood proposal

Susan / team —

Thanks for the candid conversation on Friday. Per internal discussions, Redwood can offer the following to address your commercial and reliability asks:

- 12-month reserved commit for a 4xA100-equivalent dedicated GPU pool
- 25% off list pricing on the committed spend for the term
- 1 month of free burst credits (150k token equivalent) applied during onboarding
- Throughput SLO: 10M tokens/day. If SLO misses beyond two incidents per quarter, we will credit 5% of monthly committed spend for that month (credit capped at the one-month burst value).
- Canary period: first 30 days post-launch defined as monitoring window, escalation path documented in the attached SLO appendix.

Attached: Optima_Dedicated_Offer_20270425.pdf (includes pricing worksheet and SLO appendix). We will push this to DocuSign once you confirm the commercial terms. Link to sign will follow: https://docusign.com/EX-2027-344

If you need the one-month credit to appear explicitly on invoice lines for procurement reconciliation, confirm and we'll ensure the billing flag is set.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147

Attachment: Optima_Dedicated_Offer_20270425.pdf (pricing worksheet, SLO appendix)
From: Susan Lee <susan.lee@optimahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, procurement@optimahealth.com
Date: 2027-04-29 10:12 PDT
Subject: RE: OptimaHealth counteroffer: Dedicated reserved pool — Redwood proposal

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary. OptimaHealth accepts the commercial terms as written (25% off, one month onboarding credits, throughput SLO with the described credit remedy). One remaining procurement ask: can the onboarding credit be visible as a distinct line item on the first invoice so our AP team can tie it to the PO? Also please send the finalized SLA appendix with any legal redlines early next week — our counsel will review.

Sending over a preliminary PO (see attached Optima_PO_4721.pdf). We intend to route for signature once we get the DocuSign link.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — this should let us kick off the VPC onboarding in early May.

—Susan Lee
Head of Platform Partnerships, OptimaHealth
Attachment: Optima_PO_4721.pdf
